messages:
Maya: Heads-up — saw an odd billing blip on prod around 10:12 where a reconnect + toolcall retry produced a half-charge in the console. Details below, tagging @Ashwin for routing logic and @Devon for metering heuristics.

Ashwin: ugh. can you paste the raw session/trace id?

Maya: trace=trc_8f3a, session=ssn_4422. Timeline: client open -> stream starts (prefix 120 tokens) -> intermittent network close -> client retries with resume -> server re-routes -> toolcall fired during resume -> response truncated at EOF -> two provisional ledger entries appear, each ~60 tokens.

Devon: interesting — sounds like the prefix was split across the reconnect boundary and bookkeeping created two provisional claims, then the confirmed path only reconciled one. do you have the ledger snippet?

Maya: yes — snippet from metering log (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-12T10:12:01Z] ledger: claim provisional trc_8f3a ssn_4422 prefix:120 -> provisional_id:p_9001 tokens:60
[2026-02-12T10:12:04Z] ledger: claim provisional trc_8f3a ssn_4422 resume -> provisional_id:p_9002 tokens:60
[2026-02-12T10:12:06Z] router: re-route -> region-eu -> model:rw-small-8q
[2026-02-12T10:12:07Z] toolcall: invoke tool_x trace:trc_8f3a
[2026-02-12T10:12:08Z] stream: EOF (truncated)
[2026-02-12T10:12:09Z] ledger: confirm provisional p_9001 -> confirmed c_7001 tokens:60
[2026-02-12T10:12:11Z] ledger: confirm provisional p_9002 -> confirmed c_7002 tokens:60
[2026-02-12T10:12:12Z] billing: UI shows two confirmed charges, but downstream reconciliation later merged into single usage line (60 tokens)
```

Sarah: that mismatch between console and downstream reconciliation is the UX problem. Users see two lines then a refund/merge later. we should avoid transient double-vis for customers. :grimacing:

Ashwin: root cause candidates: (1) provisional ids tied to session fragment instead of request-level id, (2) router re-route created a new provisional flow where resume logic didn't detect overlap, (3) toolcall TTL logic counted a separate provisional bucket.

Devon: +1. From metering rules, provisional claims are intentionally conservative to avoid undercharging. But we need a dedupe when overlap prefix sets are identical. maybe compare prefix hashes on resume.

Maya: I instrumented a quick query of the prefix hashes — p_9001.hash == p_9002.hash for this case. So the client retried but the router treated it as new flow.

Ashwin: ok. options: A) router: emit reuse_token when resume detected (needs session-affinity enrichment), B) metering: coalesce provisional claims with identical prefix hashes within a grace window before confirming, C) console: mark provisional rows as "provisional — may merge" and hide until reconciliation.

Devon: tradeoffs: A reduces churn but touches routing state across regions (hard). B is low-risk: coalesce on confirm path by checking overlapping provisional claims and only create one confirmed. but we still show two provisional rows to users for a short window. C is fastest for UX (label provisional + collapsible), but doesn't reduce actual double-charge noise in customer billing alerts.

Maya: customers hit support when they see spikes in console during retries. I think B+B': coalesce at confirm time and in console collapse provisional duplicates into one live provisional entry if their hashes match and timestamps within grace window (like 10s).

Sarah: +1 for console change too — even if backend coalesces, customers get less alarm if console collapses. UX proposal: add a small chevron with tooltip "merged provisional events" linking to raw trace. Also add a console filter to show only confirmed charges.

Ashwin: implementation notes: we'll need an index from provisional hash -> list of provisional_ids with timestamps. Confirm path should query that index and atomically convert the earliest provisional into confirmed and tombstone the others (generate metadata showing merged_ids). also ensure refund workflow doesn't fire.

Devon: watch out for races: if two conflicting confirms arrive concurrently (rare), we need linearization by provisional hash with lightweight lock. maybe use a CAS on the provisional-index key.

Maya: quick PoC plan: instrument a small coalesce function in the ledger service, run in canary for 48h on low-traffic region, enable console collapse flag for that org.

OpsBot: Deploy scheduled: canary/ledger-coalesce -> 2026-02-13T03:00Z (ETA 45m). @Maya @Devon tagged.

Sarah: after canary, metrics to watch: provisional-count-per-trace, provisional-confirm lag, UI provisional rows per-incident, refunds triggered. we should add a dashboard panel for "provisional merges" showing merged_count and bytes/token delta.

Ashwin: one more thought — toolcall TTL: if toolcall causes additional provisional claim during its own retry flow, we should ensure toolcall provisional gets attached to the originating provisional hash, not counted separately. patch plan: when toolcall invoked during resume, pass parent_provisional_hash header.

Maya: I'll open two PRs: ledger coalesce PoC (devon will review) and console-collapse flag (sarah will design tiny UX). I'll include the sample logs and the trace id for repro.

Devon: sounds good. assign me the ledger PR. I'll add CAS logic and unit tests covering concurrent confirms.

Sarah: I'll mock the collapsed UX and send a screenshot. small copy: "Provisional charges may be merged during reconciliation" with link to docs.

Maya: thanks — moving to action items. will update this thread with canary results. :thumbsup:
